## Overview

RDFLib.jl provides `LMDBStore`, a persistent triple store backed by [LMDB](https://www.symas.com/lmdb) (Lightning Memory-Mapped Database). It stores RDF graphs on disk with dictionary-encoded terms and sorted triple indices for fast pattern-matching queries.

```{julia}
using RDFLib
```

## Creating an LMDBStore

Open a store by providing a directory path. LMDB creates the database files automatically.

```{julia}
# Create a temporary directory for our store
db_path = mktempdir()

# Open an LMDB-backed store
store = LMDBStore(db_path)
println("Store type: ", typeof(store))
println("Store path: ", db_path)
```

## LMDB-Backed RDFGraph

Use `LMDBStore` as the backend for an `RDFGraph`.

```{julia}
# Create a graph backed by LMDB
g = RDFGraph(; store=store)
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")

# Add triples — they are written to disk immediately
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), RDF.type, ex("Person")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), RDFS("label"), Literal("Alice")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), ex("age"), Literal(30)))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), RDF.type, ex("Person")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), RDFS("label"), Literal("Bob")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), ex("knows"), ex("alice")))

println("Graph has $(length(g)) triples")
```

```{julia}
# Query works the same as any other store
results = collect(triples(g, (nothing, RDF.type, ex("Person"))))
println("People found: ", length(results))
for t in results
    println("  ", t.subject)
end
```

## Persistence Across Sessions

Data survives closing and reopening the store.

```{julia}
# Close the store
close(store)

# Reopen — data is still there
store2 = LMDBStore(db_path)
g2 = RDFGraph(; store=store2)
println("After reopen: $(length(g2)) triples")

# Verify data integrity
for t in triples(g2, (ex("alice"), nothing, nothing))
    println("  ", t.predicate, " → ", t.object)
end
```

## Bulk Loading

For loading large datasets, use `add_bulk!` which batches inserts in a single transaction for much better performance.

```{julia}
# Generate a batch of triples
bulk_triples = Triple[]
for i in 1:1000
    s = ex("item$i")
    push!(bulk_triples, Triple(s, RDF.type, ex("Item")))
    push!(bulk_triples, Triple(s, RDFS("label"), Literal("Item $i")))
    push!(bulk_triples, Triple(s, ex("value"), Literal(i)))
end

# Bulk insert — all in one transaction
count = add_bulk!(store2, bulk_triples)
println("Bulk loaded: $count triples")
println("Total: $(length(RDFGraph(; store=store2))) triples")
```

## Dictionary Encoding

LMDB store uses dictionary encoding for space efficiency. Each unique RDF term (URI, blank node, literal) is stored once and assigned a compact integer ID. Triple indices store only these IDs (3 × 8 bytes = 24 bytes per triple), making the store compact and cache-friendly.

```{julia}
# The same URI is stored once, regardless of how many triples reference it
for i in 1:100
    add!(RDFGraph(; store=store2),
        Triple(ex("new_item_$i"), RDF.type, ex("Item")))  # ex("Item") stored once
end

g3 = RDFGraph(; store=store2)
items = collect(triples(g3, (nothing, RDF.type, ex("Item"))))
println("Total items: ", length(items))
```

## Sorted Indices

`LMDBStore` maintains three sorted indices for efficient lookups:

| Index | Key Order | Best For |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| **SPO** | Subject → Predicate → Object | "What do we know about X?" |
| **POS** | Predicate → Object → Subject | "Who has property P with value V?" |
| **OSP** | Object → Subject → Predicate | "What links to X?" |

```{julia}
# Subject lookup — uses SPO index
alice_facts = collect(triples(g3, (ex("alice"), nothing, nothing)))
println("Facts about Alice: ", length(alice_facts))

# Predicate+Object lookup — uses POS index
people = collect(triples(g3, (nothing, RDF.type, ex("Person"))))
println("People: ", length(people))

# Object lookup — uses OSP index
who_knows_alice = collect(triples(g3, (nothing, ex("knows"), ex("alice"))))
println("Who knows Alice: ", length(who_knows_alice))
```

## Transactions

Wrap multiple operations in a transaction for atomicity.

```{julia}
transaction(store2) do
    g = RDFGraph(; store=store2)
    add!(g, Triple(ex("carol"), RDF.type, ex("Person")))
    add!(g, Triple(ex("carol"), RDFS("label"), Literal("Carol")))
    add!(g, Triple(ex("carol"), ex("knows"), ex("alice")))
end

g4 = RDFGraph(; store=store2)
carol_triples = collect(triples(g4, (ex("carol"), nothing, nothing)))
println("Carol facts: ", length(carol_triples))
```

## Pattern Matching

All eight query patterns (combinations of bound/unbound S, P, O) are supported efficiently.

```{julia}
g5 = RDFGraph(; store=store2)

# (?, ?, ?) — all triples
println("Total triples: ", length(g5))

# (s, ?, ?) — everything about a subject
println("Alice triples: ", length(collect(triples(g5, (ex("alice"), nothing, nothing)))))

# (?, p, ?) — all triples with a predicate
println("rdf:type triples: ", length(collect(triples(g5, (nothing, RDF.type, nothing)))))

# (?, ?, o) — all triples with an object
println("Triples pointing to Alice: ", length(collect(triples(g5, (nothing, nothing, ex("alice"))))))

# (s, p, ?) — specific subject and predicate
println("Alice's type: ", length(collect(triples(g5, (ex("alice"), RDF.type, nothing)))))
```

## Cleanup

```{julia}
close(store2)
rm(db_path; force=true, recursive=true)
println("Cleaned up")
```

## Summary

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `LMDBStore(path)` | Open/create persistent store |
| `RDFGraph(; store=store)` | Create graph backed by LMDB |
| `add!(store, triple)` | Insert a triple |
| `add_bulk!(store, triples)` | Bulk insert in one transaction |
| `triples(store, pattern)` | Pattern-matching query |
| `remove!(store, pattern)` | Remove matching triples |
| `transaction(f, store)` | Execute within transaction |
| `clear!(store)` | Clear all data |
| `close(store)` | Close the database |
